title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning - queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness and prevent request starvation under mixed workload profiles; added configurable timeouts and metrics. Default behavior is safe and non-breaking; exposes runtime knobs for advanced customers.
description: Context: We observed sustained high tail latency for small, low-token requests when mixed with large, long-running batches. Root cause: the continuous-batcher scheduler prioritized throughput and batch fullness over per-queue fairness, resulting in starvation of small-request queues and increased P99 latency. This PR implements a set of scheduler changes to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and add configurable timeouts and observability. What this PR does: introduces a priority time-slicing policy that allocates CPU/batching windows across size buckets; adds per-queue starvation timers and a head-of-line (HOL) timeout that forces flush of a partially filled batch when a request has waited beyond configured threshold; improves request-size accounting so the scheduler estimates effective batch fill by token-weighted units rather than request-count; implements early-flush heuristics driven by latency SLO signals (latency SLO breach reduces batching window to favor latency over throughput); exposes new scheduler knobs via config: scheduler.queue_time_slice_ms, scheduler.hol_timeout_ms, scheduler.token_capacity_soft_cap, scheduler.latency_slo_threshold_ms. Benchmarks & impact: microbenchmarks under a mixed workload (80% small requests, 20% large requests) show P50 latency for small requests unchanged, P95 down ~18%, P99 down ~32%. Throughput (tokens/sec) remains within 2% of baseline. Under heavy large-request load the scheduler slightly increases average latency for very large batches (~3%) in exchange for improved small-request tail latencies. Files changed (high level): updated scheduler and queueing implementation, added unit and integration tests, added metrics and docs, and a small config surface for private/dedicated deployments. See changed_files field. Testing: unit tests for scheduling logic and starvation timers, integration test that replays mixed-size traffic patterns and asserts latency SLOs, e2e bench harness used to generate the reported numbers. CI: initially flaky integration test (timeout on k8s test harness), rerun passed; full CI green before merge. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Integration test for mixed workloads - [x] Metrics added for observability (queue_length, starvation_count, hol_forced_flush) - [x] Config knobs documented in docs/continuous-batcher.md - [x] Benchmarks and a short analysis included Migration notes: defaults preserve current production behavior until rollout via config; safe to enable on Dedicated or Private clusters. Rolling restart recommended for scheduler config changes (no model artifact changes). Related: ENG-4821 (scheduling fairness investigation), ENG-4879 (production incident SUP-9123), docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/continuous-batcher (internal).

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach - can you clarify how the time-slice interacts with batching window? Specifically worried about oscillation when latency SLO toggles.
Maya Chen: Time-slice is orthogonal to batching window; we use a short-term EWMA on latency SLO breaches to avoid oscillation. Added comment and integration test to cover this scenario.
Priya Patel: Please add a metric for forced HOL flushes and expose it to the console dashboard - helpful for ops.
Maya Chen: Added hol_forced_flush counter and hooked to Console; also added dashboard tile in metrics.yaml.
Diego Ramos: Integration test was flaky earlier; after fixing k8s harness timeout I was able to reproduce benchmark results. Approving.
